title: Eromba with Ngari (Fermented Fish)
jainNotes: Contains fermented fish (ngari) - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Boiled vegetables (potato, bamboo shoot, beans, etc.)
Ngari (fermented fish), red chilli or umorok

recipe: Boil or steam seasonal vegetables until soft. Mash with roasted ngari and plenty of chilli.
Garnish with fresh maroi herbs. Serve with rice – the iconic spicy mashed side of Manipur.
tips: Ngari is the soul of Eromba – this is the classic non-vegetarian version.
Heat level can be adjusted but authentic versions are fiery.

title: Eromba (Vegetarian)
jainNotes: Contains onion and ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-ginger.

ingredients.name: Boiled vegetables (potato, bamboo shoot, beans, etc.)
Fried chives or onion, ginger, red chilli or umorok

recipe: Boil or steam seasonal vegetables until soft. Mash with fried chives/onion, ginger and plenty of chilli.
Garnish with fresh maroi herbs. Serve with rice – a vegetarian version of the iconic dish.
tips: Vegetarian version of Eromba using fried chives instead of ngari.
Still packed with flavour and heat.

title: Singju (Vegetarian)
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.

ingredients.name: Finely chopped cabbage, green papaya, other seasonal vegetables
Roasted sesame powder, gram flour, chilli, herbs, onion

recipe: Mix finely shredded vegetables with roasted sesame powder, a little gram flour, chilli, onion and local herbs.
Toss well and serve as a spicy, crunchy salad or snack.
tips: Popular street and home salad – refreshing yet spicy.
Best eaten fresh.

title: Singju with Ngari (Non-Vegetarian)
jainNotes: Contains fermented fish (ngari) and onion - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Finely chopped cabbage, green papaya, other seasonal vegetables
Roasted sesame powder, gram flour, chilli, herbs, onion

recipe: Mix finely shredded vegetables with roasted sesame powder, a little gram flour, chilli, onion and local herbs.
Add ngari. Toss well and serve as a spicy, crunchy salad or snack.
tips: Popular street and home salad with the addition of ngari.
Best eaten fresh.

title: Chamthong (Kangshoi) with Ngari
jainNotes: Contains fermented fish (ngari), onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Ngari or smoked fish, onion, ginger, garlic, chilli

recipe: Boil seasonal vegetables with onion, ginger, garlic and chilli in water to make a light stew.
Add ngari or smoked fish for flavour. Simmer briefly.
Serve with rice – an everyday light vegetable stew.
tips: Also called Kangshoi or Kangsoi – minimal oil, maximum freshness.
This is the classic non-vegetarian version with ngari.

title: Ooti
jainNotes: Contains onion and ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-ginger.

ingredients.name: Onion, ginger, baking soda or traditional alkaline water, spices

recipe: Cook rice with onion, ginger, peas or seasonal vegetables and a pinch of baking soda (or traditional khar) until soft and slightly thickened.
Season simply. Serve as a comforting one-pot vegetarian dish.
tips: Classic Meitei vegetarian preparation – the alkaline note is traditional.
Often made for religious or special occasions when non-veg is avoided.

title: Chagem Pomba
jainNotes: Contains fermented soybean (hawaijar), smoked fish, onion - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Broken rice, mustard leaves or greens
Hawaijar (fermented soybean), smoked fish, peas, onion

recipe: Cook broken rice with mustard greens, hawaijar, smoked fish, onion and peas into a thick, flavourful mixture.
Simmer till everything is soft and well combined.
Serve with rice or as a main – a hearty fermented-soybean dish.
tips: Hawaijar gives a unique fermented depth.
Mustard leaves are the preferred green.

title: Kanghou
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.

ingredients.name: Mustard oil, chilli, onion, local herbs, salt

recipe: Heat a little mustard oil, add chilli and onion and quickly stir-fry the finely chopped vegetables.
Season with salt and herbs. Keep the vegetables crisp-tender.
Serve as a dry side with rice.
tips: Simple stir-fried vegetable side – light and everyday.
Minimal oil is traditional.

title: Nga Thongba (Fish Curry)
jainNotes: Contains fish, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Mustard oil, onion, ginger, garlic, chilli, turmeric

recipe: Marinate fish with turmeric and salt. Lightly fry or cook in a gravy of onion, ginger, garlic and chilli in mustard oil.
Simmer till the fish is done. Serve with rice.
tips: Fish is central to Meitei meals.
Mustard oil and local herbs define the flavour.

title: Pork with Bamboo Shoot
jainNotes: Contains pork, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Cook pork with onion, ginger, garlic and chilli until tender. Add bamboo shoot and continue cooking till flavours meld.
Serve with rice – popular especially in hill communities and among non-Meitei groups.
tips: Bamboo shoot balances the richness of the pork.
Fermented bamboo shoot adds extra tang.

title: Kabok (Sweet Puffed Rice)
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (puffed rice, jaggery/sugar). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.
recipe: Melt jaggery with a little water until syrupy. Toss with puffed rice until well coated.
Shape into balls or leave loose. A classic sweet snack.
tips: Simple sweet puffed-rice snack enjoyed across Manipur.
Popular during festivals.

title: Kabok (Savoury Puffed Rice)
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.
recipe: Toss puffed rice with finely chopped onion, green chilli, salt and light spices.
Serve as a crunchy savoury snack.
tips: Simple savoury puffed-rice snack.
A quick and easy snack option.

title: Bora (Pakora)
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion and use Jain-compatible vegetables.

ingredients.name: Onion, green chilli, local herbs, salt

recipe: Make a batter of gram flour with chopped onion, local herbs, chilli and salt.
Deep-fry spoonfuls till golden and crisp.
Serve hot as a tea-time or evening snack.
tips: Manipuri-style fritters – often enjoyed with tea.
Best eaten fresh.

title: Morok Metpa
jainNotes: Contains fermented fish (ngari) - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Boil or roast chilli with ngari. Pound or grind into a coarse, fiery paste with garlic and salt.
Serve as a pungent side with rice and other dishes.
tips: Essential chilli-ngari chutney of Manipuri meals.
Extremely spicy – use with caution.

title: Chakhao Kheer
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (black rice, milk, sugar/jaggery, cardamom, nuts). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.

ingredients.name: Milk, sugar or jaggery, cardamom, nuts

recipe: Cook the black rice in milk with sugar or jaggery and cardamom until creamy and the rice is soft.
Garnish with nuts and raisins if desired.
Serve warm or chilled – a special dessert or festive dish.
tips: Chakhao is the aromatic black rice of Manipur – nutty and fragrant.
A prized preparation for celebrations.
